surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions involve the alternating exposure of SiCl4 and NH3 gases at different temperatures. The SiCl4 exposure at 375 °C followed by NH3 exposure at 550 °C was cyclically repeated, leading to the formation of silicon nitride through the reaction of surface species.
evidence: The SiCl4 exposure at 375 °C followed by NH3 exposure at 550 °C was cyclically repeated 20 times, leading to a silicon nitride physical thickness of ;3.5 nm as estimated from transmission electron microscopy (TEM).
